statement.excerpt: None of the current stack of AI companies can survive on their own, meaning that the venture capital industry is holding them up. If even one of these companies falters and dies, the entire narrative will die. If that happens, it will be harder for AI companies to raise, and even harder to sell an AI company to someone else.

from_speaker: None of the current stack of AI companies can survive on their own
If even one of these companies falters and dies
harder for AI companies to raise
even harder to sell an AI company
our_interpretation: The startup-financing context limits the relevant companies to AI startups operating when the post appeared, rather than established public technology companies.
The ordinary reading of surviving on their own is covering continuing operations without repeated external financing. Raising money does not itself establish that a company cannot survive without it.
A business closure following commercial failure qualifies as faltering and dying; bankruptcy is not required. Yupp qualifies under this broad reading.

The predicted death of the narrative means a broad loss of investor and buyer confidence, reflected in fundraising and acquisition conditions. Individual deals or aggregate dollar totals alone cannot establish those conditions.
The speaker supplies neither a response deadline nor a required duration. No numerical threshold or fixed waiting period is imposed.
criteria.support_condition: A qualifying post-publication startup failure is followed by broad, sustained deterioration in AI startup fundraising and acquisition conditions, with evidence connecting that deterioration to the failure. The separate universal funding-dependence premise also requires company-level financial evidence.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Following a qualifying failure, sufficiently broad evidence establishes that investor and acquisition demand remains healthy and that the asserted industry-wide loss of confidence did not occur. A verified self-financing member of the original cohort would separately contradict the universal premise.

evidence.explanation: The report establishes an announced business closure after the post. It satisfies the antecedent under the broad AI-startup reading, but not necessarily a narrower frontier-lab reading.

Continued concentration of investment in AI weighs against a simple narrative-collapse account. These U.S. year-to-date totals include investment before the closure and do not measure the ease of raising or selling individual AI startups.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A clearly qualifying failure, followed by comparable industry fundraising and acquisition evidence that establishes the predicted deterioration or decisively demonstrates its absence, together with financial evidence addressing the universal dependence premise.
